declared.title: Money and mental wellbeing: A longitudinal study of medium-sized lottery wins
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « lottery wins mental wellbeing longitudinal » (2026-11-22)

population: British Household Panel Survey: Britons with medium lottery wins (1,000 to 120,000 pounds) vs non-winners and small winners

findings.text: People who win a medium-sized lottery prize end up with better psychological health than non-winners and small winners

support.sentence: When compared to two control groups -- one with no wins and the other with small wins -- these individuals go on eventually to exhibit significantly better psychological health.

findings.text: Two years after the win, mental wellbeing is better by 1.4 points of the GHQ questionnaire

support.sentence: Two years after a lottery win, the average measured improvement in mental wellbeing is 1.4 GHQ points.

limits: playing the lottery is not random: only the size of a win among players is; one control group did not win at all
mental wellbeing (GHQ, psychological distress), not life satisfaction nor happiness
UK panel; number of winners not given in the abstract (full text not read)
